learning_objective: 🔄 Understand how cells replicate their DNA and divide to grow, heal, and reproduce through Mitosis and Meiosis!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: अंतरावस्था (विभाजन से पहले की तैयारी का चरण)
समसूत्री विभाजन (समान गुणसूत्रों वाली दो कोशिकाएं बनाना)
अर्धसूत्री विभाजन (गुणसूत्रों की संख्या आधी करके युग्मक/सेक्स सेल बनाना)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Cells spend 95% of their time in Interphase preparing to divide. It has 3 stages: G1 (cell grows), S phase (DNA replication occurs—DNA doubles, but chromosome number stays the same), and G2 (proteins are made for division).

Used for growth and repair. A diploid parent cell divides into two identical diploid daughter cells. Stages: Prophase (chromosomes condense), Metaphase (align at the equator), Anaphase (chromatids pull apart), Telophase (nuclei reform).
Used to make sperm and eggs (gametes). A diploid cell undergoes two rounds of division (Meiosis I and II) to produce four genetically different haploid cells (with half the number of chromosomes).

The longest and most complex phase of Meiosis. It has 5 stages: Leptotene, Zygotene (pairing/synapsis), Pachytene (crossing over occurs, mixing maternal and paternal genes), Diplotene (chiasmata visible), and Diakinesis.
Some cells (like adult heart cells or nerve cells) exit the G1 phase and enter an inactive state called G0. They remain metabolically active but no longer divide unless required.

fun_activity.title: 🎀 The Shoelace Chromosomes
fun_activity.instructions: Take two pairs of colored shoelaces (e.g., Red and Blue) to represent chromosomes from mom and dad. In 'Pachytene' of Meiosis, they cross over! Swap the tip of one red shoelace with a blue one. This physical mixing of genes is why you don't look exactly like your siblings!

exam_tips: 📌 DNA amount vs. Chromosome number: In the 'S' phase, the amount of DNA doubles (2C becomes 4C), but the number of chromosomes remains exactly the same (2n remains 2n).
📌 Metaphase is the best stage to observe and study the morphology (shape and number) of chromosomes under a microscope.
📌 Memorize the sequence of Prophase I: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene, Diakinesis (Mnemonic: Lazy Zebras Ponder Difficult Dreams).
quick_recap: ⭐ Mitosis maintains constant chromosome numbers across generations of cells, which is why it's called equational division.
⭐ The 'chiasmata' (X-shaped structures) become clearly visible during the Diplotene stage of Prophase I.
⭐ Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, which occurs after karyokinesis (division of the nucleus).
